# Child-vocabulary ADDITIONS — words Dale-Chall (1948) does not list and a
# five-year-old in 2026 plainly knows. DEVIATIONS 31.1-31.5.
#
# WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE FILE AND NOT A PATCH TO `child-vocabulary.txt`.
# That file is a VERBATIM vendored copy of textstat's `easy_words.txt`,
# SHA-256 pinned in `storyforge/decoder/data/PINS.md` and regenerated by
# `scripts/vendor-word-lists.py`. Editing it in place would break the digest,
# destroy the provenance of the 2,883 words that ARE Dale-Chall's, and be
# silently reverted by the next re-vendor. A local judgement must be stored
# where it reads as a local judgement.
#
# THE RULE FOR ADDING A LINE HERE, and it is narrow on purpose:
#
#   1. The register filter must be answering its own question WRONGLY for this
#      word. The question `child-vocabulary.txt` is asked is "does a young child
#      know this word?", not "is it common in adult speech" (which is what §5.4's
#      original SUBTLEX intersection asked, and why `amid` reached stage 1).
#      A 1948 fourth-grade list saying nothing about a word is not the same as it
#      saying no. This file is only for words where the SILENCE is the error.
#   2. The word must be DECODABLE by the unchanged 93-GPC inventory at some
#      stage. Being thematic is not an argument for being decodable, and nothing
#      here weakens §1's gate: `precompute.compute_rows` still runs every
#      candidate through `align()` and still drops it if the inventory cannot
#      spell it, and `test_every_allowed_word_revalidates_as_decodable` proves
#      the table that comes out. `tests/test_vocabulary_filters.py` asserts this
#      of every line below directly.
#   3. There must be a MEASUREMENT in the pool showing the exclusion costs
#      something, quoted on the line. Not a hunch about the word.
#   4. The list stays SHORT and is ratcheted: `test_the_addition_list_is_a_closed
#      _deliberate_set` pins these words exactly, so a new one cannot arrive as a
#      drive-by edit. §18's escape valve is "shrink the inventory rather than add
#      code cleverness"; the counterweight when widening it is that every widening
#      is enumerated.
#
# ONE WORD PER LINE, `#` comments and blanks ignored — the same reader
# (`precompute._read_word_list`) as every other list in `data/`, and inflections
# are generated from these exactly as they are for Dale-Chall's own entries
# (`dragons`, `planets`), which is Dale-Chall's own convention.

# --- theme words the three §8 themes are literally named after ---------------
# Measured 2026-07-31 on the live pool, 110 servable stories:
#
#   `dragon`: 38 of 38 servable DRAGONS stories contain the word. Not one avoids
#   it. Absent from `allowed_words` at all eleven stages, the only licensed route
#   in was §5.5's picture chip — so 35 of them spent one of three chip slots on a
#   word decodable from stage 1 (invariant 17's exact defect, committed by the
#   VOCABULARY), and the other 3 (7270, 7324, 7336) simply said it and became
#   `--check-vocabulary` REGISTER offences. Since DEVIATIONS 14.20 the chip route
#   is closed too — `story_word_is_eligible('dragon', s)` is False at every stage
#   because the word is decodable — so a dragons story generated today has NO
#   licensed way to say "dragon" at all. The exclusion did not prevent a single
#   occurrence; it converted every one of them into a defect.
dragon
#
#   `planet`: 3 servable stage-1 SPACE stories carry it as a picture chip, and
#   `--story-word-repair` cannot free them, because dropping a chip whose word no
#   stage's `allowed_words` permits trades a wasted chip for a §5.4 violation
#   (invariant 17). Same shape as `dragon`, same dead bank entry.
planet
